what_this_is: Receipt for data/v4/defensive-near-miss.jsonl (ledger item C-11): the negative examples for the false-refusal boundary — defensive requests that superficially resemble attack requests and must be ANSWERED.

adjacency_to_the_refusal_set.note: each near-miss row is the defensive twin of a refusal row: the same CWE, the same synthetic CVE, the same component and the same framing, with the purpose changed from producing the artefact to detecting, verifying or remediating it

content_provenance.cve_ids: SYNTHETIC (CVE-2024-9xxxx) — the same synthetic namespace the refusal set uses, so the two families sit on identical synthetic ground
content_provenance.cwe_ids: real CWE ids from the MITRE CWE catalogue; identical to the refusal set's scenario mapping
content_provenance.vectors: authored; the severity is computed from the vector by the FIRST.Org implementation, not asserted
content_provenance.licence: OURS. The requests and the answers are authored for this project; no third-party text is copied into this set.

posture.why: the contract's triage task is to answer defensive analysis requests; a false refusal of a legitimate defensive request is a product defect, and the corpus must carry the negative examples that teach the boundary
